source_review.notes: Checked all seven structured references against the current official gRPC documentation, the gRPC repository protocol specification, and RFC 9113. Core concepts supports the four method cardinalities, independent bidirectional schedules, per-call ordering, and lifecycle; PROTOCOL-HTTP2 supports one-byte compression flag, four-byte length, message framing, trailers, and grpc-status; RFC 9113 supports HTTP/2 stream multiplexing and flow control. Current flow-control, performance, keepalive, graceful-shutdown, status, error, and compression guidance supports the operational claims and is used with language/runtime qualification rather than as a universal implementation guarantee.

evidence: Checked request/response cardinalities, sequences Q_c and P_c, event predicates, transport credit W_d(t), application buffer B_d(t), limit L, half-close h_d, and terminal status T(c) for consistent domains.
Confirmed per-direction happens-before implication is explicitly conditional on delivery and does not assert ordering across calls or effects.
Confirmed unary, streaming shapes, channel, call, half-close, flow control, backpressure, terminal status, checkpoint, and pinning are defined before formal use.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates transport sequence, application buffering, durable progress, and terminal call outcome.

evidence: Enumerated {1,*} × {1,*} as exactly four method shapes: unary, server streaming, client streaming, and bidirectional streaming.
Checked the documented gRPC message prefix totals five bytes before payload: one compressed flag plus a four-byte big-endian length.
Executed the one-credit lifecycle model: the second offer blocks until one receive restores capacity, after which both messages drain before OK.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Numeric statements are protocol constants or deterministic model arithmetic; no latency, capacity, throughput, or compression benefit is claimed.

evidence: Expanded the cardinality product and mapped each ordered pair to its declared gRPC method shape.
Checked the per-direction ordering implication preserves delivered sender order within one call but cannot derive cross-direction causality or cross-call order.
Checked 0 ≤ B_d(t) ≤ L is stronger than nonnegative transport credit because eager reads can move bytes into an unbounded application queue.
Checked terminal success requires both protocol/cardinality completion and T(c)=OK rather than HTTP 200 or a nonempty response prefix.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Symbolic claims are bounded invariants over the stated call model, not exactly-once or global-order proofs.

evidence: Reviewed zero/one/many messages where the method permits, empty streams, forgotten half-close, prefix plus non-OK status, and client/server terminal disagreement.

Reviewed slow/non-reading peers, both sides writing without reads, unsupported concurrent writers, eager unbounded queues, tiny expensive messages, oversized/compressed messages, and connection-level multi-stream loss.

Reviewed restart/reconnect overlap and gaps, lost ack before/after commit, expired cursors, backend pinning/skew, drain/reconnect storms, proxy trailer/idle limits, schema skew, stale fences, and authorization changes during long streams.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Adversarial coverage spans cardinality, ordering, lifecycle races, resource exhaustion, recovery, deployment, intermediaries, and security.

evidence: The bounded-stream-lifecycle execution enforces one in-flight item, restoration on receive, explicit half-close, and OK only after the queue drains.
Confirmed every streaming recovery design uses application identity/sequence/checkpoint/deduplication rather than claiming transparent transport resumption.
Confirmed every queue, message, stream, concurrency, and decompressed-byte surface receives an explicit bounding obligation.
Confirmed per-message authorization/effect acknowledgment, backend pinning, channel reuse, graceful drain, and terminal-status observation remain explicit invariants.
invariant_checking.notes: The local model checks lifecycle structure; actual HTTP/2/gRPC/runtime behavior requires the integration and fault evidence specified by the chapter.

evidence: Reviewed the ordering argument from serial runtime writes through ordered HTTP/2-stream bytes and message reassembly, with concurrency, reconnect, and domain-commit exclusions stated.
Reviewed the counterexample showing transport flow control does not prove bounded application memory when a handler eagerly drains into an unbounded work queue.
Reviewed checkpoint recovery: durable through-k progress plus overlap and idempotent apply prevents duplicate effect, conditional on retention, identity, and gap detection.
proof_review.notes: Arguments are sound within their explicit premises and do not overclaim global ordering, completeness, or exactly-once delivery.

evidence: Confirmed official protocol guarantees are separated from language/runtime API rules and application policy.
Confirmed message write, delivery, handler read, durable commit, acknowledgment, checkpoint, and terminal status are never treated as equivalent.
Confirmed the Python lifecycle is labeled as a deterministic local model and the protobuf declaration as schematic.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Guarantee, model, mechanism, implementation, policy, and evidence labels remain distinct throughout.

evidence: Background snippet verification produced artifacts/snippets/API-053/report.json for the executable lifecycle model; its result is checked before module promotion.
The gRPC method declaration is explicitly schematic because no repository protoc/gRPC build target is required for the language-neutral contract.

Real gRPC languages, proxies, load balancers, flow-control windows, connection failures, performance, authorization systems, draining, and replication are future deployment-specific evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No live gRPC server/client, HTTP/2 proxy, load balancer, identity provider, or production stream was empirically evaluated.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed four cardinalities, wire lifecycle, ordering scope, transport versus application backpressure, half-close/status, progress acknowledgment, failure/resume, channel/pinning behavior, lifecycle/draining, security, observability, and evidence as one bounded theory-to-production treatment. API-054 retains detailed context metadata/deadline/cancellation ownership.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through explicit method selection, message framing awareness, bounded queues/streams/messages, supported concurrency patterns, checkpoint and durable ack semantics, idempotent overlap, reconnect to shared/fenced state, channel reuse, stream-aware balancing, coordinated keepalive, graceful drain, per-message authorization, protected telemetry, and real-path fault/load tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module moves from cardinality and wire lifecycle through ordering, flow control, state, recovery, placement, operations, security, and verification. Ten examples have distinct unary, incremental result, aggregate upload, bidi causality, deadlock, partial prefix, checkpoint, balancing, trailer, and authorization purposes; five exercises progress to safety-critical regional replication.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
